title: Signed area and regions below the axis
problem: Evaluate $\displaystyle\int_0^{2\pi} \sin x\,dx$ and explain the result geometrically.

steps.instruction: Find the antiderivative and apply the limits.

steps.working: The definite integral is zero, but the curve is not zero everywhere. On $[0, \pi]$, $\sin x \geq 0$ (area above the axis), and on $[\pi, 2\pi]$, $\sin x \leq 0$ (area below the axis). The two areas are equal in magnitude, so they cancel: $$\int_0^{\pi}\sin x\,dx = 2 \qquad \text{and} \qquad \int_{\pi}^{2\pi}\sin x\,dx = -2$$ Key point: the definite integral gives signed area. To find the total enclosed area, integrate on each sub-interval separately and add the absolute values.

answer: $\displaystyle\int_0^{2\pi} \sin x\,dx = 0$, since the equal positive and negative signed areas cancel.

title: Applying the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus

steps.instruction: Apply the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus: if $G(x) = \displaystyle\int_a^x f(t)\,dt$, then $G'(x) = f(x)$.

steps.working: $$G'(2) = \frac{1}{2^2 + 1} = \frac{1}{5}$$ Note that the lower limit $a = 2$ plays no role in the derivative — only the integrand evaluated at the upper limit matters.
